source.title: On Some Open Problems in Many-Electron Theory

accepted.question_text: For an interacting many-electron physical system with electron-nuclear attraction potential v(r), if the exact ground-state density ρ(r) is given, is there a closed-form expression for the ground-state energy Egs purely in terms of ρ(r) and v(r)?

evidence.quote: • Is there a closed form expression for ground-state energy from ground-state density?

For the interacting physical system of interest, assume that one is given the exact ground-state density, ρ(r), associated with electron-nuclear attraction potential v(r). Is there a closed-form expression that gives the ground-state energy, Egs, in terms of ρ(r) and v(r)?

accepted.question_text: For Coulomb systems, is the ionization energy always greater than the electron affinity? Equivalently, does the ionization energy sequence always satisfy I[N + 1] < I[N], where I[M] denotes the ionization energy of the M-electron system?

evidence.quote: • Is the Ionization Energy always greater than the Electron Affinity for Coulomb systems?

To my knowledge there is no proof that the ionization energy is always greater than the electron affinity for Coulomb systems, even though this property is so very important in the study of band gaps and strong corre￾lations. In other words, there does not appear to be a general proof that I[N + 1] < I[N] where I[M] is the ionization energy of the M-electron system.

accepted.question_text: Let Ψ_N be an N-particle wave function with one-particle density ρΨ(x), exchange-correlation energy Exc, and local kinetic-energy density TΨ(x). Can one prove a lower bound for Exc that depends on both TΨ(x) and ρΨ(x), using the local ratio between TΨ(x) and the minimum kinetic-energy density of a free Fermi gas with the same particle density, so that the bound locally reduces to the Dirac exchange-correlation expression when that ratio is small and has effective constant CLO when that ratio is large?
accepted.context_brief: Exchange-correlation lower bound with kinetic density

evidence.quote: The first term on the right side is called the direct energy and the difference between it and the left side of (2) is called the exchange- correlation energy and is denoted by Exc. Thus, (2) gives a lower bound to Exc and the goal is to improve it.
We may define the kinetic energy density as the positive function TΨ (x) = N ∫ |∇xΨ(x, x2, . . . , xN )|^2 dx2 · · · dxN .

OPEN PROBLEM: Find a lower bound to Exc that involves both TΨ (x) and ρΨ (x) by using the ratio RΨ (x) = TΨ (x) / [ (3/5)(6π^2)^(2/3) q^(-2/3) ρΨ (x)^(5/3) ] to improve the LO type bound (or some other bound) in a way that (locally) reduces to the Dirac Exc when RΨ (x) is small. When RΨ (x) is large the effective constant (locally) should be CLO.
